Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "物出新參照，致重繪。useMemo .Wrap之。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

1: # Open CVN
2: 
3: ## Descripcion
4: 
5: Este repositorio contiene un Trabajo de Fin de Grado orientado a definir un
6: esquema de datos abierto para la representacion de curriculos en el ambito
7: universitario y de investigacion en Espana, tomando como punto de partida el
8: formato CVN.
9: 
10: El problema de partida es que, aunque el CVN existe como formato normalizado,
11: la elaboracion, mantenimiento y adaptacion de curriculos a distintos contextos
12: sigue consumiendo mucho tiempo y dificulta el desarrollo de herramientas
13: abiertas interoperables. Una de las causas es la ausencia de una definicion de
14: bajo nivel suficientemente clara para representar y procesar estos datos.
15: 
16: ## Objetivo Del Proyecto
17: 
18: El objetivo general del TFG es definir un esquema de datos que permita la
19: gestion automatizada de curriculos academicos y de investigacion en Espana.
20: 
21: Ese objetivo se descompone en varias lineas de trabajo:
22: 
23: 1. estudiar el formato CVN actual y analizar sus limitaciones
24: 2. proponer un formato de bajo nivel agnostico respecto al formato final de
25:    representacion
26: 3. definir un esquema final basado en JSON, apto para ficheros de texto y bases
27:    de datos NoSQL
28: 4. desarrollar una aplicacion en Python para lectura y validacion de curriculos
29:    utilizando Pydantic
30: 5. desarrollar herramientas de almacenamiento local y exportacion a LaTeX
31: 6. explorar el uso de LLM para importar curriculos generados por herramientas
32:    externas como la aplicacion de la FECYT
33: 
34: ## Alcance Actual Del Repositorio
35: 
36: La infraestructura que actualmente se esta construyendo para generar modelos
37: Pydantic es solo una parte del proyecto total. En esta fase, el foco del
38: repositorio esta en sentar la base tecnica del pipeline que permitira:
39: 
40: 1. traducir los artefactos oficiales CVN XML/XSD a bindings estructurales
41:    Pydantic
42: 2. normalizar la metadata funcional y tecnica del paquete oficial
43: 3. generar mas adelante modelos de dominio reutilizables y un esquema final mas
44:    limpio
45: 
46: Esta base es necesaria para el parser/validador en Python, pero no agota el TFG:
47: todavia quedan por delante la definicion del modelo final, la capa JSON, la
48: exportacion a LaTeX, y la futura exploracion de una herramienta de importacion
49: basada en LLM.
50: 
51: ## Direccion Tecnica Actual
52: 
53: El repositorio sigue una arquitectura de dos capas:
54: 
55: 1. bindings estructurales generados a partir del paquete oficial CVN
56: 2. modelos semanticos y de dominio que se generaran sobre metadata normalizada
57: 
58: La arquitectura, el estado actual y el roadmap se documentan en el propio
59: repositorio para que futuras sesiones no dependan de reconstruir el contexto a
60: partir del chat o de issues externos.
61: 
62: ## Punto De Entrada
63: 
64: Para obtener el contexto del proyecto y el estado real de implementacion, leer:
65: 
66: 1. `PROJECT_GUIDE.md`
67: 2. `docs/context/project_context_index.md`
68: 3. `docs/context/current_status.md`
69: 
70: ## Documentos Clave
71: 
72: - guia principal del proyecto:
73:   `PROJECT_GUIDE.md`
74: - indice de contexto del proyecto:
75:   `docs/context/project_context_index.md`
76: - estado actual del proyecto:
77:   `docs/context/current_status.md`

79:   `docs/pipeline/cvn_pydantic_generation_pipeline.md`
80: - roadmap completo:
81:   `docs/roadmap/cvn_generation_roadmap.md`
82: - guia de contribucion y setup:
83:   `CONTRIBUTING.md`
84:

1: # Project Guide
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This file is the human entry point for understanding the repository.
6: It summarizes the project purpose, the current implementation focus, the
7: documentation structure, and the repository rules that matter to contributors
8: and maintainers.
9: 
10: ## What This Repository Is
11: 
12: This repository contains a Trabajo de Fin de Grado focused on defining an open
13: data schema for representing academic and research CVs in Spain, taking the
14: CVN format as the starting point.
15: 
16: The long-term goal is not only to mirror the official CVN package, but to make
17: curriculum data easier to validate, transform, store, and export through open
18: tooling.
19: 
20: ## Current Technical Scope
21: 
22: The repository is currently centered on the generation pipeline that turns the
23: official CVN XML/XSD package into reproducible Python artifacts.
24: 
25: Current and planned layers are:
26: 
27: 1. structural bindings generated from the official CVN XML/XSD package
28: 2. normalized metadata extracted from the official supporting XML documents
29: 3. semantic mapping rules that recover domain meaning from the structural layer
30: 4. domain-oriented Pydantic models built over normalized metadata
31: 
32: This means the repository is currently implementing the technical foundation
33: for the future parser, validator, JSON-oriented schema, and downstream export
34: work. It is not yet the full end-user CV tooling envisioned by the TFG.
35: 
36: ## Recommended Reading Order For Humans

1: # Issue 43 - Define Agnostic Conceptual Model Extraction Layer
2: 
3: ## Summary
4: 
5: Issue `#43` defines an intermediate representation for agnostic curriculum
6: concepts derived from the generated/domain Pydantic layer and CVN trace metadata.
7: 
8: This issue is part of epic `#41`.
9: 
10: ## Goal
11: 
12: - define a conceptual model inventory that is not tied to XML serialization,
13:   Python implementation details, or generated module structure
14: - preserve traceability to CVN codes, XML paths, reference resolution, and
15:   semantic policy decisions
16: - create the source layer from which UML and JSON schema work can proceed
17: 
18: ## Background
19: 
20: The current domain generator emits traceable Pydantic artifacts, but the TFG
21: requires a representation that describes curriculum concepts rather than CVN XML
22: mechanics. A conceptual IR should sit between generated Pydantic models and
23: diagram/schema outputs.
24: 
25: ## Proposed Conceptual IR Contents
26: 
27: The IR should represent:
28: 
29: - conceptual entities
30: - attributes
31: - relationships
32: - controlled vocabularies and reference families
33: - required/optional status
34: - cardinality
35: - value type
36: - source CVN code trace
37: - source XML path trace when relevant
38: - semantic policy decision trace
39: - known limitations or unresolved cases
40: 
41: ## Planned Steps
42: 
43: 1. inspect available domain generation metadata and `cvn_trace` values
44: 2. define dataclasses or typed records for conceptual entities, fields,
45:    relationships, vocabularies, and trace data
46: 3. decide grouping rules by curriculum domain areas instead of raw XML packages
47: 4. map representative generated Pydantic fields into the conceptual IR
48: 5. define deterministic ordering and stable identifiers
49: 6. document which XML/Python details must be excluded from conceptual output
50: 7. add tests if implementation is authorized
51: 
52: ## Expected Output
53: 
54: - conceptual IR contract under `src/cvn_codegen/` if implementation is approved
55: - documentation of mapping rules from generated/domain metadata into the IR
56: - representative inventory for at least personal data and one academic/research
57:   section

# Skill: caveman

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |
| **ultra** | Abbreviate (DB/auth/config/req/res/fn/impl), strip conjunctions, arrows for causality (X → Y), one word when one word enough |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully 文言文. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (之/乃/為/其) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop → new ref → re-render. `useMemo`."
- wenyan-lite: "組件頻重繪，以每繪新生對象參照故。以 useMemo 包之。"
- wenyan-full: "物出新參照，致重繪。useMemo .Wrap之。"
- wenyan-ultra: "新參照→重繪。useMemo Wrap。"

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."
- ultra: "Pool = reuse DB conn. Skip handshake → fast under load."
- wenyan-full: "池reuse open connection。不每req新開。skip handshake overhead。"
- wenyan-ultra: "池reuse conn。skip handshake → fast。"

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

<content>
1: # CVN Pydantic Generation Pipeline
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This document describes the technical architecture of the CVN generation
6: pipeline and the current structural implementation baseline.
7: 
8: ## Canonical Source Package
9: 
10: The canonical source package is:
11: 
12: ```text
13: docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/
14: |- Leeme.txt
15: |- LeemeENTITY.txt
16: |- LeemeREFERENCETABLES.txt
17: |- LeemeTHESAURUS.txt
18: |- CVN_README.md
19: |- Manual/
20: |  |- Manual de Especificaciones Técnicas v1.4.3_v2.1.pdf
21: |  |- TreeModel_v1.0 20090331 v1.0.pdf
22: |  |- Entidades_esquema_Entity_v1.4.xsd_2008-07-04 v1.0.pdf
23: |  |- ReferenceTables.pdf
24: |  |- Subtypes_v1.1.pdf
25: |  `- Tesauros 2008-01-23 v1.0.pdf
26: |- XML/
27: |  |- SpecificationManual.xml
28: |  |- CVNTreeModel.xml
29: |  |- Entity.xml
30: |  |- ReferenceTables.xml
31: |  |- Subtype_Spa.xml
32: |  |- Thesaurus.xml
33: |  |- Thesaurus_Eng.xml
34: |  `- Thesaurus_Spa.xml
35: `- XSD/
36:    |- CVN.xsd
37:    |- Common.xsd
38:    |- AuxTable.xsd
39:    |- ISOUtilities.xsd
40:    |- SpecificationManual.xsd
41:    |- CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd
42:    |- Entity_v1.4.xsd
43:    |- EntityUtilities_v1.4.xsd
44:    |- ISOUtilitiesENTITY.xsd
45:    |- CVNUtilities_v1.0.xsd
46:    |- ReferenceTables.xsd
47:    |- ISOUtilitiesREFERENCETABLES.xsd
48:    |- Subtypes.xsd
49:    |- Thesaurus.xsd
50:    `- ISOUtilitiesTHESAURUS.xsd
51: ```
52: 
53: These artifacts represent three different but related layers, plus a set of
54: auxiliary catalog families that the core CVN package references indirectly.
55: 
56: ### Layer 1 - Final CVN XML Structure
57: 
58: - `XSD/CVN.xsd` defines the XML exchanged by CVN systems
59: - root element: `CVN`
60: - main blocks: `Version`, `Agent`, repeated `CvnItem`
61: 
62: ### Layer 2 - Technical Reusable Types And Controlled Values
63: 
64: - `XSD/Common.xsd` defines wrappers such as `CVN_string`, `CVN_date`,
65:   `CVN_ISO_639`, `CVN_ISO_3166`, and `FlexibleDatesType`
66: - `XSD/AuxTable.xsd` defines CVN auxiliary controlled values
67: - `XSD/ISOUtilities.xsd` defines ISO code tables reused elsewhere
68: 
69: ### Layer 3 - Functional And Technical Metadata
70: 
71: - `XML/SpecificationManual.xml` is the functional manual in XML form
72: - `XML/CVNTreeModel.xml` maps functional CVN codes to technical XML paths
73: - `XSD/SpecificationManual.xsd` validates the manual XML
74: - `XSD/CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd` validates the tree model XML
75: 
76: ### Layer 4 - Auxiliary Catalog Families
77: 
78: - `XML/Entity.xml` and `XSD/Entity_v1.4.xsd` define a normalized institution and
79:   organization registry used by CVN through references such as
80:   `ENTITY@Entity.xsd`
81: - `XML/ReferenceTables.xml` and `XSD/ReferenceTables.xsd` materialize a large
82:   portion of the Annex I auxiliary tables in XML form
83: - `XML/Subtype_Spa.xml` and `XSD/Subtypes.xsd` define the codification layer for
84:   `Subtype` values derived from auxiliary tables
85: - `XML/Thesaurus.xml`, `XML/Thesaurus_Eng.xml`, `XML/Thesaurus_Spa.xml`, and
86:   `XSD/Thesaurus.xsd` define the hierarchical keyword thesaurus referenced from
87:   fields such as `THESAURUS@thesaurus.xsd`
88: 
89: ## Observed Relationships Between Files
90: 
91: - `XSD/CVN.xsd` includes `Common.xsd` and `AuxTable.xsd`
92: - `XSD/Common.xsd` includes `ISOUtilities.xsd`
93: - `XSD/SpecificationManual.xsd` imports the CVN namespace for language typing
94: - `XSD/CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd` uses its own namespace
95: - `XML/SpecificationManual.xml` is validated by `XSD/SpecificationManual.xsd`
96: - `XML/CVNTreeModel.xml` is validated by `XSD/CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd` in
97:   principle, although a documented inconsistency exists in practice
98: - `XML/Entity.xml` is validated by `XSD/Entity_v1.4.xsd` in conceptual terms,
99:   although the preserved repository layout differs from the relative
100:   `schemaLocation` strings used in the original files
101: - `XML/ReferenceTables.xml` is validated by `XSD/ReferenceTables.xsd`
102: - `XML/Subtype_Spa.xml` is validated by `XSD/Subtypes.xsd`
103: - `XML/Thesaurus*.xml` is validated by `XSD/Thesaurus.xsd`
104: 
105: The conceptual relationship is:
106: 
107: ```text
108: SpecificationManual.xml
109:   -> functional meaning of CVN codes
110: 
111: CVNTreeModel.xml
112:   -> technical mapping of those codes into XML nodes and paths
113: 
114: CVN.xsd + Common.xsd + AuxTable.xsd + ISOUtilities.xsd
115:   -> valid XML structure and controlled value types
116: 
117: Entity.xml + Entity_v1.4.xsd + helpers
118:   -> normalized external entity registry used by CVN references
119: 
120: ReferenceTables.xml + ReferenceTables.xsd
121:   -> machine-readable auxiliary tables corresponding to Annex I
122: 
123: Subtype_Spa.xml + Subtypes.xsd
124:   -> codification bridge from auxiliary table values to `Subtype`
125: 
126: Thesaurus.xml + Thesaurus.xsd
127:   -> hierarchical multilingual keyword vocabulary
128: ```
129: 
130: ## Observed Structural Characteristics
131: 
132: ### Complexity Snapshot
133: 
134: - `CVN.xsd`: 74 `complexType`, 232 `element`, 125 `attribute`, 3 `choice`
135: - `Common.xsd`: 11 `complexType`, 1 `choice`
136: - `AuxTable.xsd`: 33 `simpleType`
137: - `ISOUtilities.xsd`: large enumerations for ISO codes
138: 
139: ### Relevant Structural Friction
140: 
141: - recursion through `Link -> CvnItemType`
142: - repeated wrappers using `Item` plus metadata attributes
143: - a small number of important `choice` constructs
144: - very large enums
145: 
146: ### Metadata Coverage
147: 
148: - `SpecificationManual.xml`: 1456 `Item` elements and 1456 unique codes
149: - `CVNTreeModel.xml`: 101 `CVNItem`, 939 `Property`, 4635 `Indicator`
150: - `CVNTreeModel.xml`: 1430 unique codes
151: - overlap between manual and tree model: 1429 codes
152: - codes in manual but not tree model: 27
153: - code in tree model but not manual: `030.010.000.250`
154: 
155: ### Reference Table Situation
156: 
157: Resolvable internally in the core or auxiliary package:
158: 
159: - `ISO_3166`
160: - `ISO_639`
161: - tables in `AuxTable.xsd`
162: - tables in `ReferenceTables.xml`
163: - `UNESCO_CODES`
164: 
165: Available as side-package registries rather than direct core XSD enums:
166: 
167: - `ENTITY@Entity.xsd` -> represented by `Entity_v1.4.xsd` and `Entity.xml`
168: - `THESAURUS@thesaurus.xsd` -> represented by `Thesaurus.xsd` and
169:   `Thesaurus*.xml`
170: 
171: Still unresolved or requiring explicit semantic policy:
172: 
173: - some manual references do not map cleanly to a side-package table from the
174:   package alone, for example `CVN_AGENCY_C`
175: 
176: ## Architecture Decision
177: 
178: The repository uses a two-layer architecture:
179: 
180: ```text
181: Official XSDs
182:   -> structural Pydantic bindings
183: 
184: SpecificationManual.xml + CVNTreeModel.xml
185:   + optional CVN.xsd/Common.xsd structural type trace
186:   -> normalization
187:   -> semantic mapping rules and overrides
188:   -> domain Pydantic models
189: ```
190: 
191: This means:
192: 
193: - `src/generated/` is an interoperability layer
194: - future semantic cleanup belongs outside `src/generated/`
195: - `SemanticPolicyBundle` is the source of truth for generator semantics
196: - the domain generator must not re-derive semantic policy from raw XML, raw XSD,
197:   or generated structural bindings
198: 
199: The complete implemented handoff is:
200: 
201: ```text
202: normalized metadata + auxiliary reference resolution + structural type evidence
203: -> SemanticPolicyBundle
204: -> domain generator
205: -> domain-oriented Pydantic artifacts
206: ```
207: 
208: ### Current Normalization Entry Point
209: 
210: - the recommended repository entry point for normalized metadata is:
211:   - `cvn_codegen.normalization.build_normalization_result(...)`
212: - this entry point returns the integrated normalization layer used by later
213:   roadmap issues, including:
214:   - normalized entries by CVN code
215:   - tree entries by technical XML path
216:   - optional structural type evidence when `cvn_xsd_path` and `common_xsd_path`
217:     are provided
218:   - source-exclusive code sets
219:   - currently documented mismatch reporting
220: - canonical domain generation provides `CVN.xsd` and `Common.xsd` to this entry
221:   point so wrapper policies can be attached without generator-side raw XSD
222:   inspection
223: - lower-level helper functions inside `cvn_codegen.normalization` remain
224:   importable when needed, but they are not the preferred integration surface for
225:   later stages
226: 
227: ## Repository Layout
228: 
229: ```text
230: src/
231: ├── generated/
232: │   ├── cvn/
233: │   ├── reference_tables/
234: │   ├── subtypes/
235: │   ├── entity/
236: │   ├── specification_manual/
237: │   ├── thesaurus/
238: │   └── tree_model/
239: ├── cvn_codegen/
240: └── models/
241:     └── cvn/
242: ```
243: 
244: ### Responsibilities
245: 
246: - `src/generated/`: generated structural bindings
247: - `src/cvn_codegen/`: hand-maintained loading, normalization, resolution,
248:   semantic-policy, and generation logic
249: - `src/models/cvn/components.py`: hand-maintained shared domain components
250: - `src/models/cvn/generated/`: generated domain-oriented model output
251: 
252: Do not edit `src/generated/` manually. Regenerate it from the canonical XSDs.
253: 
254: Do not edit `src/models/cvn/generated/` manually. Regenerate it through the
255: domain generator.
256: 
257: ## Complete Regeneration Workflow
258: 
259: The contributor-facing workflow is documented in:
260: 
261: - `docs/development/regeneration_workflow.md`
262: 
263: The command sequence is:
264: 
265: ```bash
266: uv sync --group codegen --group testing
267: uv pip install -e .
268: uv run python -m cvn_codegen.xsdata_runner all
269: uv run python -m cvn_codegen.domain_model_generator
270: uv run pytest -n auto tests
271: ```
272: 
273: The implemented workflow stages are:
274: 
275: 1. core structural binding generation from `CVN.xsd`,
276:    `SpecificationManual.xsd`, and `CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd`
277: 2. auxiliary structural binding generation from `ReferenceTables.xsd`,
278:    `Subtypes.xsd`, `Entity_v1.4.xsd`, and `Thesaurus.xsd`
279: 3. normalization of `SpecificationManual.xml` and `CVNTreeModel.xml`
280: 4. auxiliary-source loading and deterministic reference-resolution enrichment
281: 5. XSD-enriched structural type evidence for wrapper handoff
282: 6. semantic policy application over enriched normalized metadata
283: 7. domain model generation under `src/models/cvn/generated/`
284: 8. local and CI verification through `uv run pytest -n auto tests`
285: 
286: ### Controlled-Reference Source Order
287: 
288: Normalization materializes controlled-reference meaning before semantic policy
289: consumes it. The effective source-of-truth order is:
290: 
291: 1. explicit side-package references such as `ENTITY@Entity.xsd` and
292:    `THESAURUS@thesaurus.xsd`
293: 2. direct `ReferenceTables.xml` matches where applicable
294: 3. subtype-backed classification through `Subtype@Subtypes.xsd`
295: 4. hierarchical thematic classification where technical metadata supports it
296: 5. unresolved documented exceptions and under-traced tables
297: 
298: Representative cases include `CVN_SEX_A`, `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE`, `CVN_KNOW_A`,
299: `ENTITY@Entity.xsd`, `THESAURUS@thesaurus.xsd`, `UNESCO_CODES`, `CVN_AGENCY_C`,
300: `CVN_INTERVENTION_A`, and `CVN_PRUEBA`.
301:

1: # Known Limitations
2: 
3: ## Purpose
4: 
5: This document records known limitations of the current pipeline so later issues
6: do not need to rediscover them.
7: 
8: ## Structural Binding Limitations
9: 
10: ### `xs:choice` Is Not Enforced As Mutual Exclusivity
11: 
12: - Affected areas include:
13:   - `FlexibleDatesType`
14:   - `OfficialIdType`
15:   - `EntityTypeType`
16:   - `EntityNameType`
17: - Impact:
18:   - generated Pydantic models may accept states that are invalid with respect to
19:     the source XSD
20: - Expected follow-up:
21:   - issue `#14` defines the semantic policy
22:   - issue `#15` should restore domain-facing semantics
23: 
24: ### Wrapper Type Evidence Requires XSD-Enriched Normalization
25: 
26: - Affected wrapper families include:
27:   - `FlexibleDatesType`
28:   - `OfficialIdType`
29:   - `EntityTypeType`
30:   - `EntityNameType`
31: - Confirmed behavior:
32:   - hotfix `#8` adds typed `StructuralTypeEvidence` to the normalized handoff
33:     when normalization receives `cvn_xsd_path` and `common_xsd_path`
34:   - canonical domain generation provides those XSD paths and can attach wrapper
35:     policy without scanning raw XSD files inside generator logic
36:   - normalization calls that omit XSD paths preserve backward-compatible empty
37:     structural evidence and therefore cannot attach wrapper-aware field shapes
38: - Impact:
39:   - canonical issue `#15` generation can consume wrapper-aware domain shapes
40:   - custom callers that need wrapper attachment must use the XSD-enriched
41:     normalization path
42: - Expected follow-up:
43:   - issue `#16` should keep regression coverage for both enriched wrapper
44:     handoff behavior and no-XSD backward-compatible behavior
45: 
46: ### `minOccurs` Is Not Enforced For Generated Lists
47: 
48: - Generated list fields with `default_factory=list` do not enforce the minimum
49:   cardinality implied by the XSD
50: - Impact:
51:   - empty lists may be accepted in object construction even when the XSD
52:     expects at least one element
53: - Expected follow-up:
54:   - issue `#14` records semantic cardinality policy
55:   - issue `#15` should decide concrete generated validation behavior
56: 
57: ### Some Attributes Are Typed As `object`
58: 
59: - Seen in parts of `specification_manual` and `tree_model`
60: - Impact:
61:   - validation is weaker than the XSD suggests
62:   - ergonomics are worse for downstream code
63: - Expected follow-up:
64:   - issue `#14` defines semantic treatment outside generated bindings
65:   - issue `#15` should avoid leaking weak structural types into domain models
66: 
67: ### XML Helper Types Are Less Ergonomic Than Primitives
68: 
69: - Wrappers such as `CVN_duration`, `CVN_gYear`, and `CVN_gYearMonth` map to XML
70:   helper types such as `XmlDuration` and `XmlPeriod`
71: - Impact:
72:   - structural fidelity is preserved, but programmatic usage is more delicate
73: - Expected follow-up:
74:   - issue `#14` defines semantic base-kind policy
75:   - issue `#15` should map these cases into usable domain-facing shapes
76: 
77: ## Generation Process Limitations
78: 
79: ### `tree_model` Needs A Target-Specific xsdata Override
80: 
81: - Default structural generation hit circular dependency problems
82: - Current workaround:
83:   - `--unnest-classes`
84: - Impact:
85:   - generation is reproducible, but not uniform across all three targets
86: - Expected follow-up:
87:   - keep documented through issue `#17`
88: 
89: ## Canonical Source Package Inconsistencies
90: 
91: ### `CVNTreeModel.xml` Diverges From `CVNTreeModel_v1.0.xsd`
92: 
93: - Confirmed discrepancy:
94:   - the XML includes `<Type>` inside `Indicator`
95:   - the XSD only declares `Value` and `Child` inside `Indicator`
96: - Confirmed scope of the discrepancy:
97:   - the canonical XML contains `438` `Indicator` nodes with
98:     `mo:name="Type"`, which is compatible with the documented tree-model
99:     structure
100:   - only `2` real child elements named `<Type>` were found in the canonical XML
101:   - those `2` unexpected child elements appear under:
102:     - `Indicator mo:name="Type" mo:code="060.030.070.220"`
103:     - `Indicator mo:name="Type" mo:code="060.030.070.230"`
104:   - both unexpected child elements contain the value:
105:     `CVN_QualityTypeType@AuxTable.xsd`
106: - Comparison with the tree-model documentation:
107:   - `TreeModel_v1.0 20090331 v1.0.pdf` defines `Indicator` children as only
108:     `Value` and `Child`
109:   - the document does not describe `<Type>` as an allowed child element of
110:     `Indicator`
111:   - this makes the two `<Type>` elements a source inconsistency, not a
112:     documented feature of the tree model
113: - Practical consequence:
114:   - the generated `tree_model` binding is correct with respect to the XSD, but
115:     cannot fully parse the canonical XML file
116: - Normalization consequence:
117:   - issue `#13` should treat `xml_path` as a structural path built from
118:     `CVNTreeModel`, `Node`, `CVNItem`, `Property`, and `Indicator`
119:   - the unexpected `<Type>` child elements should be recorded as explicit
120:     mismatches or special-case findings, not folded into the standard structural
121:     path model
122: - Parse status:
123:   - `SpecificationManual.xml`: parse OK
124:   - `CVNTreeModel.xml`: parse blocked by XML/XSD mismatch
125: - Expected follow-up:
126:   - issue `#13` must treat the tree-model XML as a source of truth for
127:     normalization even when the XSD does not describe it completely
128: 
129: ### Auxiliary Catalog Families Preserve Historical Packaging Drift
130: 
131: - affected families:
132:   - `Entity`
133:   - `ReferenceTables/Subtypes`
134:   - `Thesaurus`
135: - confirmed issues:
136:   - XML `schemaLocation` values assume colocated XSD files, while the preserved
137:     repository package stores XML and XSD in separate directories
138:   - several `Leeme*.txt` files mention filenames that do not exactly match the
139:     preserved repository filenames, such as `Subtypes.xml` instead of
140:     `Subtype_Spa.xml`, or lowercase thesaurus filenames that differ from the
141:     actual files
142:   - side families duplicate ISO helper schemas instead of using one fully shared
143:     physical artifact
144:   - `Subtypes` materials preserve version drift between PDF, XSD, and XML files
145: - impact:
146:   - package exploration and automated file resolution cannot rely on filenames or
147:     relative schema locations alone
148:   - tooling must resolve these families through repository-aware path mapping and
149:     documented semantic relationships
150: - expected follow-up:
151:   - issue `#14` defines semantic policy for side-package references
152:   - issue `#15` should decide which of these auxiliary artifacts become domain
153:     sources versus support registries
154: 
155: ### Some Annex-I Table References Remain Unresolved From The Package Alone
156: 
157: - confirmed example:
158:   - `CVN_AGENCY_C` appears referenced from the manual material but does not map
159:     cleanly to a matching table in `ReferenceTables.xml`
160: - impact:
161:   - not every table name from the manual can yet be promoted to a strict
162:     machine-resolved enum or closed catalog using the source package alone
163: - expected follow-up:
164:   - issue `#14` defines open versus closed treatment for unresolved tables
165:   - issue `#15` should preserve such cases as explicit external or manual-only
166:     references unless stronger evidence is introduced
167: 
168: ### `Subtype_Spa.xml` Does Not Provide A Direct Table-Family Bridge
169: 
170: - confirmed behavior:
171:   - `Subtype_Spa.xml` can be parsed and used to prove subtype catalog
172:     availability
173:   - the preserved XML is keyed by numeric subtype item codes such as `001`,
174:     `002`, and not by reference-table family names such as `CVN_KNOW_A`
175: - impact:
176:   - the current normalization layer can classify tables as subtype-backed and
177:     record that subtype catalog data is available, but it does not yet verify a
178:     strict per-table-family bridge directly from `Subtype_Spa.xml`
179: - expected follow-up:
180:   - issue `#14` treats subtype-backed families as enum-ineligible until stronger
181:     bridge evidence exists
182:   - later maintenance work may add a stricter bridge only if reliable evidence
183:     is introduced from the preserved source package
184: 
185: ### Strict Enum Eligibility Is Evidence-Backed But Conservative
186: 
187: - confirmed behavior:
188:   - hotfix `#7` adds per-table enum evidence from `ReferenceTables.xml` to the
189:     normalization-to-semantic handoff
190:   - issue `#14` now evaluates strict enum eligibility through typed evidence such
191:     as item count, code stability, label quality, hierarchy, delegate/open
192:     behavior, duplicate values, blank values, and other-like entries
193:   - compact direct tables can become `EnumEligibility.ELIGIBLE` when evidence
194:     shows a small closed table, as with `CVN_SEX_A`
195:   - compact tables with delegate/open-world behavior remain strict-enum
196:     ineligible, as with `CVN_ENTITY_TYPE` and `delegate_present`
197: - impact:
198:   - issue `#15` may generate strict enums only when semantic policy reports
199:     `EnumEligibility.ELIGIBLE`
200:   - `EnumEligibility.REVIEW_REQUIRED` and `EnumEligibility.INELIGIBLE` must not
201:     be treated as final strict-enum permission
202: - expected follow-up:
203:   - issue `#15` should consume the dynamic eligibility result without
204:     re-inspecting `ReferenceTables.xml`
205:   - future explicit overrides, if any, must remain versioned `OverrideRule` data
206:     rather than hidden table-name branches
207: 
208: ## Documentation Rule
209: 
210: Whenever a new limitation is discovered, add it here and reference the issue
211: expected to address it.

(End of file - total 211 lines)
</content>

450: 
451: ## Research Summary
452: 
453: ### Current Domain Model Inventory
454: 
455: The current generated domain layer is large enough that direct class diagrams over
456: Python code are likely to become unreadable without curation.
457: 
458: Observed inventory from `src/models/cvn/generated/` and
459: `src/models/cvn/components.py`:
460: 
461: - generated Python files excluding `__init__.py`: `104`
462: - generated domain model classes: `103`
463: - generated enum classes: `13`
464: - shared component classes: `17`
465: - generated domain model fields: `1487`
466: - generated model field count range: `1` to `48`
467: - average generated model fields: `14.44`
468: 
469: Representative large generated models include:
470: 
471: - `FormacionAcademicaImpartida`: `48` fields
472: - `ProyectosDeIDIFinanciadosEnConvocatoriasCompetitivasDeAdministracionesOEntidadesPublicasYPrivadas`:
473:   `35` fields
474: - `PublicacionesDocumentosCientificosYTecnicos`: `33` fields
475: - `ContratosConveniosOProyectosDeIDINoCompetitivosConAdministracionesOEntidadesPublicasOPrivadas`:
476:   `32` fields
477: - `PropiedadIndustrialEIntelectual`: `32` fields
478: 
479: The generated model layer is useful as an implementation and traceability source,
480: but it still reflects CVN item grouping and generator naming decisions. That makes
481: it unsuitable as the final conceptual UML source by itself.
482: 
483: ### Pydantic Metadata Findings
484: 
485: Pydantic v2 model metadata can expose useful structural facts:
486: 
487: - class names
488: - field names
489: - field annotations
490: - required versus optional status
491: - repeated fields through `list[...]` annotations and `default_factory=list`
492: - referenced shared value objects, such as `EntityNameValue`, `EntityTypeValue`,
493:   `FlexibleDateValue`, `OfficialIdValue`, `HierarchicalCodeReference`,
494:   `VocabularyReference`, and other controlled-reference components
495: - JSON Schema `$defs` for shared component references
496: 
497: Pydantic metadata is not enough for the conceptual target because:
498: 
499: - generated classes are grouped by CVN item/module shape, not stable curriculum
500:   concepts
501: - field-level CVN trace is not emitted into the generated Python field metadata
502:   even though generator IR records field trace internally
503: - relationships between conceptual entities such as `Person`, `Curriculum`,
504:   `EducationalExperience`, `ProfessionalSituation`, or `Publication` cannot be
505:   reliably inferred from annotations alone
506: - controlled-reference semantics are visible only as emitted component types or
507:   enums, while the richer decision evidence lives upstream in normalized metadata
508:   and `SemanticFieldPolicy`
509: 
510: ### Pyreverse Evaluation
511: 
512: Pyreverse can generate DOT class diagrams from repository Python modules and can
513: be useful for implementation diagnostics.
514: 
515: A tiny local experiment was run outside tracked repository outputs:
516: 
517: ```text
518: uvx --from pylint pyreverse --output dot --project cvn_sample --output-directory /tmp/opencode src/models/cvn/generated/cvn_item_010_010_000_000.py src/models/cvn/components.py
519: ```
520: 
521: Temporary outputs:
522: 
523: - `/tmp/opencode/classes_cvn_sample.dot`
524: - `/tmp/opencode/packages_cvn_sample.dot`
525: 
526: Observed result:
527: 
528: - Pyreverse emitted class records and inheritance edges.
529: - Shared Pydantic implementation details such as `model_config` appeared in the
530:   diagram.
531: - Generated class attributes appeared, but many component relationships were not
532:   promoted to clear UML associations.
533: - The output remained Python/package-centric rather than curriculum-domain-centric.
534: 
535: Conclusion:
536: 
537: - Pyreverse is not recommended as the final UML generation path.
538: - Pyreverse may remain useful as a temporary diagnostic tool for Python dependency
539:   or inheritance inspection.
540: 
541: ### PlantUML Evaluation
542: 
543: PlantUML is a strong target for generated conceptual diagrams because it supports:
544: 
545: - classes, enums, abstract classes, stereotypes, and notes
546: - package and namespace grouping
547: - associations, dependencies, inheritance, composition, and aggregation
548: - labels and cardinalities on relations
549: - field-level and link-level notes
550: - hiding, removing, tagging, and splitting large diagrams
551: - text-first source files that can be versioned deterministically
552: 
553: PlantUML is the best fit when the repository needs expressive UML-like output for
554: the TFG explanation and for diagrams grouped by curriculum domain area.
555: 
556: Primary limitation:
557: 
558: - rendering requires PlantUML-compatible tooling or a viewer, although raw `.puml`
559:   files can remain the canonical versioned source.
560: 
561: ### Mermaid Evaluation
562: 
563: Mermaid class diagrams support:
564: 
565: - classes and class members
566: - relationships and multiplicities
567: - namespaces
568: - annotations such as `<<Enumeration>>` and `<<Abstract>>`
569: - notes
570: - Markdown fenced-code rendering on GitHub
571: 
572: Mermaid is useful as a lightweight repository-native publication target, because
573: GitHub renders Mermaid diagrams directly in Markdown contexts.
574: 
575: Primary limitation:
576: 
577: - Mermaid is less expressive than PlantUML for heavily annotated, large,
578:   traceability-rich UML documentation.
579: 
580: ### Custom Pydantic Introspection Evaluation
581: 
582: A custom extractor over generated Pydantic classes could extract a technical
583: model graph containing:
584: 
585: - generated model class
586: - field name
587: - field type
588: - required/optional flag
589: - repeated/single flag
590: - enum reference
591: - shared component reference
592: 
593: This can help issue `#43` bootstrap evidence, but it should not be the only source
594: of truth for the conceptual model. The extractor must be combined with normalized
595: metadata and semantic policy data to recover CVN code trace, source references,
596: domain-shape decisions, wrapper policies, controlled-reference families, and
597: semantic confidence.
598: 
599: ### Conceptual IR Evaluation
600: 
601: The recommended direction is a conceptual intermediate representation before any
602: diagram rendering.
603: 
604: Issue `#43` should define an IR that represents:
605: 
606: - conceptual entities
607: - conceptual fields or attributes
608: - relationships and relationship cardinality
609: - value types
610: - controlled vocabularies and reference families
611: - required/optional and repeated/single status
612: - CVN code trace
613: - XML path trace when useful
614: - semantic policy decision trace
615: - unresolved or weakly supported cases
616: 
617: The IR should exclude:
618: 
619: - raw generated module names such as `cvn_item_050_020_010_000`
620: - Python inheritance details such as `BaseCvnDomainModel`
621: - Pydantic implementation details such as `model_config` and `Field(...)`
622: - raw XML wrapper mechanics except where they map to stable value objects
623: - one-class-per-CVN-code or one-class-per-CVN-item output when that obscures the
624:   curriculum concept
625: 
626: ## Comparison Matrix
627: 
628: | Option | Readability | Domain agnosticism | Traceability | Automation fit | Recommendation |
629: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
630: | Pyreverse over generated Python | Low for final docs | Low | Low to medium | Medium | Diagnostic only |
631: | Custom direct Pydantic introspection | Medium | Low to medium | Medium if enriched | Medium | Auxiliary input only |
632: | Conceptual IR plus PlantUML | High | High | High | High | Primary path |
633: | Conceptual IR plus Mermaid | Medium to high | High | Medium | High | Secondary publication path |
634: 
635: ## Final Recommendation
636: 
637: ### Decision: Do Not Generate Final UML Directly From Python Classes
638: 
639: Final UML or UML-like diagrams should not be generated directly from the generated
640: Pydantic class layer.
641: 
642: Reason:
643: 
644: - direct Python diagrams preserve implementation shape, generated module names,
645:   Pydantic details, and CVN item grouping
646: - the TFG needs an agnostic curriculum model, not a diagram of generated Python
647:   files
648: - the information needed for good conceptual diagrams spans generated Pydantic
649:   code, normalized metadata, semantic policy, and CVN trace data
650: 
651: ### Decision: Use A Conceptual IR From Issue `#43`
652: 
653: Issue `#43` should define and, if authorized, implement a conceptual extraction
654: layer. That layer should consume the existing domain generation evidence and
655: semantic handoff instead of re-deriving meaning from raw XML/XSD files or relying
656: only on Python annotations.
657: 
658: Recommended sources for issue `#43`:
659: 
660: - `NormalizationResult`
661: - `NormalizedCodeEntry`
662: - `SemanticFieldPolicy`
663: - `SemanticDecisionTrace`
664: - `DomainGenerationResult` or equivalent generator evidence when field grouping
665:   and emitted shape are needed
666: - generated Pydantic classes only as a validation or convenience source
667: 
668: ### Decision: Use PlantUML As Primary Diagram Target
669: 
670: Issue `#44` should use PlantUML as the primary rendering target because it best
671: supports expressive class diagrams, packages, stereotypes, notes, cardinality,
672: and trace annotations.
673: 
674: Recommended output shape for issue `#44`:
675: 
676: - versioned `.puml` sources as canonical diagram artifacts
677: - diagrams grouped by curriculum domain areas, not generated Python packages
678: - optional rendered images only if tooling is added and documented
679: 
680: ### Decision: Keep Mermaid As Secondary Markdown Target
681: 
682: Mermaid should be considered a secondary output for smaller, reader-friendly
683: diagrams embedded in Markdown, especially where GitHub-native rendering matters.
684: 
685: Mermaid should not be the only target if the project needs dense trace notes,
686: large package diagrams, or richer visual styling.
687: 
688: ## Risks And Limitations
689: 
690: - Generated Pydantic models are too numerous and too implementation-oriented for
691:   direct final UML.
692: - Pyreverse diagrams can include Pydantic implementation details and miss useful
693:   conceptual associations from type annotations.
694: - Pydantic metadata alone does not preserve enough field-level CVN trace in the
695:   current generated files.
696: - Conceptual relationships require curation; they cannot be inferred perfectly
697:   from generated field annotations.
698: - Controlled vocabularies can overload diagrams if all values are rendered inline.
699: - PlantUML adds an external rendering dependency if rendered images are required.
700: - Mermaid is convenient in GitHub Markdown but less expressive for large,
701:   trace-heavy UML documentation.
702: 
703: ## Impact On Issue `#43`
704: 
705: Issue `#43` should proceed with the conceptual IR approach. It should not treat
706: generated Python classes as the final conceptual schema. It should define explicit
707: records for curriculum entities, fields, relationships, vocabulary references,
708: cardinality, and trace data.
709: 
710: ## Impact On Issue `#44`
711: 
712: Issue `#44` should render diagrams from the issue `#43` conceptual IR. It should
713: prefer PlantUML as the primary target and optionally generate Mermaid diagrams for
714: small Markdown-friendly views.
715: 
716: ## Verification
717: 
718: - confirm research references are recorded
719: - confirm recommendation is explicit enough for issue `#43` to start
720: - no code implementation required unless a tiny local experiment is explicitly
721:   approved
722: 
723: ## Verification Performed
724: 
725: - Research references are recorded in this issue document.
726: - Generated domain model inventory was measured from the current repository.
727: - A tiny local Pyreverse experiment was run under `/tmp/opencode` only; no tracked
728:   repository output was created.
729: - The recommendation is explicit: use a conceptual IR for issue `#43`; do not use
730:   direct generated Python diagrams as final UML.
731: - The recommended primary target for issue `#44` is PlantUML.
732: - Mermaid is recorded as a secondary Markdown-friendly target.
733: - No productive code implementation was added.
734: 
735: ## Impact On Later Issues
736: 
737: - issue `#43` uses the chosen extraction direction
738: - issue `#44` uses the chosen diagram rendering target
739: 
740: ## Status
741: 
742: - Status: completed

51: ) -> dict[str, tuple[NormalizedCodeEntry, ...]]:
52:     grouped: dict[str, list[NormalizedCodeEntry]] = {}

59:             continue

70:         group_key: tuple(grouped[group_key])
71:         for group_key in sorted(grouped)

247: def build_group_key_class_suffix(group_key: str) -> str:
248:     if group_key.startswith("__") and group_key.endswith("__"):
249:         tokens = tuple(
250:             token
251:             for token in re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", " ", group_key).split()
252:             if token
253:         )
254:         if not tokens:
255:             return "Group"
256:         return "".join(token.capitalize() for token in tokens)
257: 
258:     suffix = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "", group_key)
259:     return suffix or "Group"

262: def resolve_generation_unit_class_name_collisions(
263:     units: tuple[DomainGenerationUnit, ...],
264: ) -> tuple[DomainGenerationUnit, ...]:
265:     grouped_by_class_name: dict[str, list[DomainGenerationUnit]] = defaultdict(list)
266:     for unit in units:
267:         grouped_by_class_name[unit.class_name].append(unit)
268: 
269:     resolved_units: list[DomainGenerationUnit] = []
270:     used_class_names: set[str] = set()
271: 
272:     for class_name in sorted(grouped_by_class_name):
273:         grouped_units = sorted(
274:             grouped_by_class_name[class_name],
275:             key=lambda unit: (unit.source_group_key, unit.module_name),
276:         )
277: 
278:         if len(grouped_units) == 1 and class_name not in used_class_names:
279:             resolved_units.append(grouped_units[0])
280:             used_class_names.add(class_name)
281:             continue
282: 
283:         for index, unit in enumerate(grouped_units, start=1):
284:             base_suffix = build_group_key_class_suffix(unit.source_group_key)
285:             candidate_class_name = f"{unit.class_name}{base_suffix}"
286:             if candidate_class_name in used_class_names:
287:                 candidate_class_name = f"{candidate_class_name}{index}"
288: 
289:             resolved_units.append(
290:                 DomainGenerationUnit(
291:                     module_name=unit.module_name,
292:                     class_name=candidate_class_name,
293:                     source_group_key=unit.source_group_key,
294:                     fields=unit.fields,
295:                 )
296:             )
297:             used_class_names.add(candidate_class_name)
298: 
299:     return tuple(sorted(resolved_units, key=lambda unit: unit.module_name))

353: def build_enum_member_name(
354:     preferred_label: str,
355:     code_value: str,
356: ) -> str:
357:     normalized_label = normalize_ascii_text(preferred_label).upper()
358:     normalized_label = re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]+", "_", normalized_label).strip("_")
359:     if normalized_label and not normalized_label[0].isdigit():
360:         return normalized_label
361:     normalized_code = re.sub(r"[^A-Z0-9]+", "_", code_value.upper()).strip("_")
362:     if not normalized_code:
363:         normalized_code = "UNKNOWN"
364:     return f"CODE_{normalized_code}"

366: def get_enum_evidence_from_entry(
367:     entry: NormalizedCodeEntry,
368: ) -> tuple[ReferenceTableEnumEvidence | None, str | None]:
369:     reference_resolution = entry.reference_resolution
370:     if reference_resolution is None:
371:         return None, None
372:     source_reference = (
373:         reference_resolution.resolved_name
374:         or reference_resolution.raw_reference
375:         or entry.code
376:     )
377:     evidence = reference_resolution.reference_table_enum_evidence
378:     if evidence is None:
379:         return None, source_reference
380:     return evidence, source_reference

382: def build_domain_enum_spec(
383:     policy: SemanticFieldPolicy,
384:     evidence: ReferenceTableEnumEvidence,
385:     source_reference: str,
386: ) -> DomainEnumSpec:
387:     members_with_labels = sorted(
388:         zip(evidence.normalized_codes, evidence.preferred_labels),
389:         key=lambda item: item[0],
390:     )
391:     members = tuple(
392:         (
393:             build_enum_member_name(
394:                 preferred_label=preferred_label,
395:                 code_value=code_value,
396:             ),
397:             code_value,
398:         )
399:         for code_value, preferred_label in members_with_labels
400:     )
401:     labels = {
402:         code_value: preferred_label
403:         for code_value, preferred_label in members_with_labels
404:     }
405:     return DomainEnumSpec(
406:         class_name=build_enum_class_name(policy),
407:         source_reference=source_reference,
408:         members=members,
409:         labels=labels,
410:         trace={
411:             "code": policy.code,
412:             "xml_paths": policy.xml_paths,
413:             "source_reference": source_reference,
414:             "domain_shape_kind": policy.domain_shape_kind.value,
415:             "enum_eligibility": policy.enum_eligibility.value,
416:         },
417:     )

419: def build_enum_specs_for_entries(
420:     entries: tuple[NormalizedCodeEntry, ...],
421:     policy_index: dict[str, SemanticFieldPolicy],
422: ) -> tuple[DomainEnumSpec, ...]:
423:     enum_specs_by_source_reference: dict[str, DomainEnumSpec] = {}
424:     for entry in sorted(entries, key=lambda item: item.code):
425:         policy = policy_index[entry.code]
426:         if not should_emit_enum_for_policy(policy):
427:             continue
428:         evidence, source_reference = get_enum_evidence_from_entry(entry)
429:         if evidence is None or source_reference is None:
430:             continue
431:         if source_reference in enum_specs_by_source_reference:
432:             continue
433:         enum_specs_by_source_reference[source_reference] = build_domain_enum_spec(
434:             policy=policy,
435:             evidence=evidence,
436:             source_reference=source_reference,
437:         )
438:     return tuple(
439:         sorted(
440:             enum_specs_by_source_reference.values(),
441:             key=lambda enum_spec: enum_spec.class_name,
442:         )
443:     )

775: def normalize_ascii_text(value: str) -> str:
776:     """Normalize text to ASCII-compatible identifier input."""
777: 
778:     normalized_value = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", value)
779:     return normalized_value.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
780: 
781: def build_snake_case_identifier(value: str) -> str:
782:     """Build a deterministic snake_case identifier from a label."""
783:     normalized_value = normalize_ascii_text(value)
784:     identifier_parts: list[str] = []
785:     current_part: list[str] = []
786:     for character in normalized_value:
787:         if character.isalnum():
788:             current_part.append(character.lower())
789:             continue
790:         if current_part:
791:             identifier_parts.append("".join(current_part))
792:             current_part = []
793:     if current_part:
794:         identifier_parts.append("".join(current_part))
795:     identifier = "_".join(identifier_parts)
796:     if not identifier:
797:         return "unnamed"
798:     if identifier[0].isdigit():
799:         return f"field_{identifier}"
800:     return identifier
801: 
802: def build_pascal_case_identifier(value: str) -> str:
803:     """Build a deterministic PascalCase identifier from a label."""
804:     snake_case_identifier = build_snake_case_identifier(value)
805:     parts = tuple(
806:         part
807:         for part in snake_case_identifier.split("_")
808:         if part
809:     )
810:     if not parts:
811:         return "Unnamed"
812:     pascal_parts = tuple(
813:         part.upper() if part in PRESERVED_ACRONYMS else part.capitalize()
814:         for part in parts
815:     )
816:     return "".join(pascal_parts)
817:

820: def select_naming_source_label(entry: NormalizedCodeEntry) -> str:
821:     """Select the best available label for domain-facing naming."""
822:     manual_entry = entry.manual
823:     if manual_entry is None:
824:         return entry.code
825:     if manual_entry.manual_name:
826:         return manual_entry.manual_name
827:     if manual_entry.manual_short_name:
828:         return manual_entry.manual_short_name
829:     return entry.code

831: def build_naming_policy(entry: NormalizedCodeEntry) -> NamingPolicy:
832:     """Build the naming policy for one normalized entry."""
833:     source_label = select_naming_source_label(entry)
834:     normalized_field_name = build_snake_case_identifier(source_label)
835:     normalized_class_name = build_pascal_case_identifier(source_label)
836:     return NamingPolicy(
837:         normalized_field_name=normalized_field_name,
838:         normalized_class_name=normalized_class_name,
839:         naming_confidence=PolicyConfidence.MEDIUM,
840:         source_label=source_label,
841:         notes=(
842:             "Spanish-first naming source selected from normalized manual metadata.",
843:         ),
844:     )

2: 
3: ## Summary
4: 
5: Epic `#41` continues the project after the CVN generation workflow baseline. Its
6: goal is to move from generated Pydantic artifacts toward the TFG objective: an
7: agnostic curriculum data model, a JSON-oriented schema, and a parser/validator
8: that can import CVN data from PDF, XML, and JSON sources.
9: 
10: This epic must not treat the current generated Pydantic models as the final
11: conceptual model. They are an implementation source and traceability layer. The
12: domain model must remain agnostic to XML serialization details.
13: 
14: ## TFG Alignment
15: 
16: This epic addresses these TFG phases:
17: 
18: 1. propose a low-level format independent from the final representation
19: 2. define a JSON-based schema for text files and NoSQL-like storage
20: 3. develop a Python parser and validator using Pydantic
21: 4. prepare the base for later local storage, LaTeX export, and application work
22: 
23: The guiding principle remains:
24: 
25: - do not model CVN XML structure as the domain
26: - recover curriculum concepts and preserve CVN traceability
27: - keep XML, JSON, UML, and Pydantic as representations over a shared semantic
28:   model
29: 
30: ## Problem Statement
31: 
32: The repository now has structural bindings, normalized metadata, semantic policy,
33: domain generation, and tests. The next problem is to decide how those generated
34: models can support a representation that is useful beyond Python code:
35: 
36: - a UML or UML-like diagram for agnostic conceptual representation
37: - a JSON Schema suitable as the project exchange and persistence schema
38: - a parser/validator capable of importing existing CVN material and validating
39:   it against the new model
40: 
41: ## Research Scope
42: 
43: ### Pydantic To UML Or UML-Like Representation
44: 
45: Research how to transform many Pydantic classes into a diagram that is useful for
46: agnostic modeling.
47: 
48: Candidate approaches include:
49: 
50: - code-analysis tools such as Pyreverse for Python class diagrams
51: - text diagram formats such as PlantUML or Mermaid class diagrams
52: - a custom extractor over Pydantic model metadata
53: - a custom conceptual intermediate representation that removes Python/XML noise
54:   before rendering UML
55: 
56: The research must explicitly compare code-centric diagrams with conceptual
57: domain diagrams. If code-centric tools produce noisy output, the epic should
58: prefer an intermediate conceptual model and generate UML from that.
59: 
60: ### Pydantic To JSON Schema
61: 
62: Research and implement JSON Schema generation from the domain Pydantic layer.
63: 
64: Relevant Pydantic v2 entry points include:
65: 
66: - `BaseModel.model_json_schema()`
67: - `TypeAdapter.json_schema()`
68: - `pydantic.json_schema.models_json_schema(...)`
69: 
70: The expected schema baseline is JSON Schema Draft 2020-12, aligned with the
71: current Pydantic JSON Schema support.
72: 
73: ### Parser And Validator Inputs
74: 
75: The parser/validator must support these input families:
76: 
77: 1. CVN PDF generated by FECYT, extracting embedded XML when available
78: 2. CVN XML directly
79: 3. Open CVN JSON directly
80: 
81: The PDF path should first attempt deterministic XML extraction from embedded
82: files or PDF metadata. OCR or LLM-based PDF reconstruction is not part of the
83: first parser acceptance path unless explicitly planned later.
84: 
85: ## Architecture Direction
86: 
87: The intended architecture is:
88: 
89: ```text
90: generated domain Pydantic models + trace metadata
91: -> conceptual model inventory
92: -> agnostic UML/diagram representation
93: -> JSON Schema generation
94: -> parser/validator for PDF/XML/JSON inputs
95: ```
96: 
97: The parser direction is:
98: 
99: ```text
100: PDF CVN -> extract embedded XML -> XML import path
101: XML CVN -> structural parse -> normalized/domain mapping -> Pydantic validation
102: JSON CVN -> JSON Schema/Pydantic validation -> domain object
103: ```
104: 
105: ## Planned Work Items
106: 
107: The detailed issue records for this epic are:
108: 
109: - issue `#42`: `docs/roadmap/issues/issue-42-research-pydantic-to-uml-options.md`
110: - issue `#43`: `docs/roadmap/issues/issue-43-agnostic-conceptual-model-extraction-layer.md`
111: - issue `#44`: `docs/roadmap/issues/issue-44-generate-uml-or-uml-like-diagrams.md`
112: - issue `#45`: `docs/roadmap/issues/issue-45-generate-json-schema-from-domain-models.md`
113: - issue `#46`: `docs/roadmap/issues/issue-46-define-canonical-open-cvn-json-format.md`
114: - issue `#47`: `docs/roadmap/issues/issue-47-unified-parser-validator-contract.md`
115: - issue `#48`: `docs/roadmap/issues/issue-48-cvn-pdf-xml-extraction.md`
116: - issue `#49`: `docs/roadmap/issues/issue-49-xml-json-import-validation.md`
117: - issue `#50`: `docs/roadmap/issues/issue-50-parser-workflow-tests-and-documentation.md`
118: 
119: ### Issue `#42` - Research Pydantic-To-UML Options
120: 
121: - compare Pyreverse, PlantUML, Mermaid, and custom extraction approaches
122: - decide whether UML should be generated from Python code directly or from a
123:   conceptual intermediate representation
124: - document tradeoffs for huge generated model sets
125: 
126: ### Issue `#43` - Define Agnostic Conceptual Model Extraction Layer
127: 
128: - define an intermediate representation for curriculum concepts
129: - consume generated Pydantic/domain metadata and CVN trace data
130: - remove Python, XML, and generated-code noise where it is not domain meaning
131: - preserve CVN `code`, XML path, reference resolution, and semantic policy trace
132: 
133: ### Issue `#44` - Generate UML Or UML-Like Diagrams
134: 
135: - emit PlantUML or Mermaid diagrams from the conceptual model inventory
136: - group diagrams by curriculum domain areas rather than raw XML packages
137: - include cardinality, composition, controlled references, and trace notes where
138:   useful
139: 
140: ### Issue `#45` - Generate JSON Schema From Domain Models
141: 
142: - generate JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 from the domain Pydantic layer
143: - decide validation vs serialization schema mode
144: - preserve useful `$defs` and references
145: - add CVN trace metadata where appropriate
146: - document limitations in generated JSON Schema
147: 
148: ### Issue `#46` - Define Canonical Open CVN JSON Format
149: 
150: - define root object shape, metadata, versioning, and extension strategy
151: - decide how CV sections and repeated entries are represented
152: - decide how CVN trace identifiers survive in JSON
153: - define compatibility rules for future schema versions
154: 
155: ### Issue `#47` - Define Unified Parser And Validator Contract
156: 
157: - define common parser result and error types
158: - expose import functions for PDF, XML, and JSON inputs
159: - normalize validation errors across input formats
160: - document public API boundaries
161: 
162: ### Issue `#48` - Implement CVN PDF XML Extraction
163: 
164: - inspect FECYT CVN PDFs for embedded XML or XML metadata
165: - extract XML deterministically when present
166: - report unsupported PDF cases clearly when XML cannot be recovered
167: - leave OCR or LLM reconstruction for later explicit planning
168: 
169: ### Issue `#49` - Implement XML And JSON Import Validation
170: 
171: - import direct CVN XML through existing structural and domain layers
172: - import Open CVN JSON through Pydantic and JSON Schema validation
173: - preserve traceability from source input to domain output
174: - provide tests for valid and invalid inputs
175: 
176: ### Issue `#50` - Add Tests And Documentation For Parser Workflow
177: 
178: - add fixtures for XML, JSON, and PDF-with-embedded-XML when available
179: - test parser contracts and error reporting
180: - document commands and examples for contributors
181: - update current status, roadmap, and known limitations
182: 
183: ## Expected Outputs
184: 
185: - research record for Pydantic-to-UML options
186: - documented conceptual intermediate representation
187: - generated UML or UML-like diagrams for the agnostic model
188: - generated JSON Schema for the Open CVN format
189: - parser/validator API for PDF, XML, and JSON import
190: - tests and contributor documentation
191: 
192: ## Parser Import Contract
193: 
194: The parser should eventually expose a clear contract similar to:
195: 
196: - `parse_cvn_pdf(...)`
197: - `parse_cvn_xml(...)`
198: - `parse_open_cvn_json(...)`
199: - `validate_open_cvn_json(...)`
200: 
201: All paths should return a common result shape with:
202: 
203: - parsed domain data
204: - source format
205: - validation status
206: - trace metadata
207: - structured errors or warnings
208: 
209: ## Known Risks
210: 
211: - Python class diagrams may be too implementation-heavy for agnostic UML
212: - generated Pydantic models may expose too much CVN/XML structure
213: - PDF CVN XML extraction depends on how FECYT embeds or stores XML in PDFs
214: - JSON Schema may need custom generation to preserve semantic trace and version
215:   metadata cleanly
216: - XML import may need explicit mapping from structural CVN XML to the domain JSON
217:   shape
218: 
219: ## Out Of Scope
220: 
221: - full desktop or web application implementation
222: - SQLite persistence
223: - LaTeX export and PDF rendering
224: - LLM-based import from PDFs without embedded XML
225: - manual editing UI for curriculum versions
226: 
227: Those concerns belong to the later application epic.
228: 
229: ## Status
230: 
231: - Status: planned
232: - Details for child issues should be expanded when epic `#41` starts

(End of file - total 232 lines)
</content>

1: # Propuesta de modelado UML + OCL para CVN
2: 
3: ## Objetivo
4: 
5: Este documento propone una estrategia practica para traducir el material de `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025` a un modelo **UML + OCL** agnostico al lenguaje y desacoplado de la serializacion XML.
6: 
7: El objetivo no es copiar el XML CVN en UML, sino construir un **modelo conceptual de dominio** reutilizable que:
8: 
9: - represente el significado real de la informacion curricular
10: - pueda serializarse despues a CVN-XML
11: - permita definir restricciones semanticas con OCL
12: - mantenga trazabilidad con los codigos CVN originales
13: 
14: ---
15: 
16: ## Principio de modelado
17: 
18: ## Regla principal
19: 
20: No modelar **la estructura XML** como si fuera **el dominio**.
21: 
22: En CVN hay que separar tres cosas:
23: 
24: 1. **Conceptos del dominio curricular**
25: 2. **Restricciones de negocio**
26: 3. **Mecanismo tecnico de intercambio XML**
27: 
28: En consecuencia:
29: 
30: - el **UML** debe representar conceptos del dominio
31: - el **OCL** debe capturar reglas semanticas
32: - el **mapeo a XML** debe quedar en una capa aparte
33: 
34: ---
35: 
36: ## Fuentes que debes usar
37: 
38: ## Fuentes principales para el modelo conceptual
39: 
40: - `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/Manual/Manual de Especificaciones Técnicas v1.4.3_v2.1.pdf`
41: - `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/XML/SpecificationManual.xml`
42: - `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/XSD/AuxTable.xsd`
43: - `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/XSD/ISOUtilities.xsd`
44: 
45: ## Fuentes secundarias para trazabilidad tecnica
46: 
47: - `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/XML/CVNTreeModel.xml`
48: - `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/XSD/CVN.xsd`
49: - `docs/CvnXML_v1.4.3_2.1_17012025/Manual/TreeModel_v1.0 20090331 v1.0.pdf`
50: 
51: ## Interpretacion recomendada
52: 
53: - `Manual PDF` -> semantica de negocio
54: - `SpecificationManual.xml` -> catalogo estructurado de campos
55: - `AuxTable.xsd` -> codelists y enumeraciones
56: - `CVNTreeModel.xml` -> mapeo tecnico campo -> XML
57: - `CVN.xsd` -> validacion estructural del XML final
58: 
59: ---
60: 
61: ## Lo que no conviene hacer
62: 
63: ## Error 1. Partir de `CVN.xsd`
64: 
65: Si el UML nace del XSD, el resultado tendera a ser XML-centrico:
66: 
67: - `Title`
68: - `Description`
69: - `Entity`
70: - `Date`
71: - `Subject`
72: - `Filter`
73: 
74: Eso es util para serializacion, pero pobre como modelo de dominio.
75: 
76: ## Error 2. Convertir cada codigo CVN en una clase
77: 
78: Los codigos CVN son muy buenos para trazabilidad y documentacion, pero no necesariamente equivalen a clases conceptuales.
79: 
80: Ejemplo:
81: 
82: - `000.010.000.010` y `000.010.000.020` no deben generar clases independientes; son atributos de una entidad `Person` o `PersonalIdentification`.
83: 
84: ## Error 3. Tomar el arbol de `CVNTreeModel` como ontologia del dominio
85: 
86: Ese arbol es un modelo de codificacion tecnica, no un modelo conceptual neutral.
87: 
88: ---
89: 
90: ## Estrategia general recomendada
91: 
92: ## Vision en 4 capas
93: 
94: ### Capa A. Modelo conceptual UML
95: 
96: Contiene clases de dominio limpias y estables.
97: 
98: ### Capa B. Restricciones OCL
99: 
100: Contiene reglas semanticas, de obligatoriedad y coherencia.
101: 
102: ### Capa C. Codelists y vocabularios controlados
103: 
104: Representa catálogos como paises, idiomas, tipos de entidad, etc.
105: 
106: ### Capa D. Mapeo a CVN
107: 
108: Relaciona clases y atributos UML con:
109: 
110: - codigo CVN
111: - tabla de referencia CVN
112: - elemento XML CVN si procede
113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## Proceso de trabajo sugerido
117: 
118: ## Fase 1. Extraer el inventario conceptual
119: 
120: Debes recorrer el manual y agrupar campos por conceptos de negocio, no por estructura XML.
121: 
122: ### Ejemplo
123: 
124: Los campos:
125: 
126: - apellidos
127: - nombre
128: - sexo
129: - nacionalidad
130: - fecha de nacimiento
131: 
132: deben llevarte a una entidad tipo `Person` o `PersonalIdentification`.
133: 
134: ## Fase 2. Detectar entidades transversales reutilizables
135: 
136: Muchas partes de CVN reutilizan patrones comunes:
137: 
138: - entidad organizativa
139: - localizacion
140: - periodo temporal
141: - identificador digital
142: - publicacion
143: - palabras clave
144: 
145: Esas piezas no deben duplicarse por modulo.
146: 
147: ## Fase 3. Construir paquetes UML
148: 
149: Agrupa por areas funcionales y por reutilizacion.

152:

155: ## Fase 5. Añadir restricciones OCL
156:

158: 
159: - obligatoriedad simple
160: - obligatoriedad condicional
161: - coherencia temporal

163:

165:

174: ---
